content.text: I'll price the example plan with a 5% price increase to show the churn impact.

With a 5% price increase on the example plan, churn itself doesn't change—it remains at 200 bps (2% monthly, assumed) [E1]. However, the price rise improves margin economics: adjusted margin over 12 months grows from 333703 cents to 360614 cents, a gain of 26911 cents despite the same churn rate [E1]. The survival rate stays at 7848 bps (78.48%) because churn probability is independent of pricing in this model [E1]. In practice, raising prices typically increases churn, but that would require a separate elasticity assumption.
